Cost of Capture Sensitivity Analysis. Marginal improvements in the performance of the structured sorbent filter result in a compounded reduction in the cost of capture of CO . For example, a small improvement in the adsorption rate and CO capacity 2 2 significantly lowers capital costs due to fewer filter modules and reduces OPEX for the facility’s balance of plant, reducing the cost of CO removal from $241/tCO to $217/tCO . While external factors like 2 2 2 electricity costs also influence economics, simultaneous improvements in adsorption rate, sorbent capacity, and manufacturing could result in a cost of CO removal as low as $165/tCO . 2 2 Task 6 – Life-cycle Assessment The same facility operating at a 100,000 TPY scale at a capacity factor of 85% underwent a life-cycle analysis prepared in accordance with ISO 14040/14044 requirements and the NETL CO2U LCA Guidance Document as modified by the 45Q addendum to determine the net CO capture potential of the technology. 2 The LCA report was provided to DOE and included as an addendum to this final report. This study was conducted as a cradle-to-grave analysis normalized to the basis of 1 kg CO captured from 2 the atmosphere and permanently stored in a saline aquifer.
